title: Keeping Living Tissue Alive in a Dish

scenes.tts: Every specimen Cajal studied was fixed. A row of fibres of different lengths could show stages of one fibre growing, or old fibres becoming visible. Someone had to watch a fibre while it was alive. Inside a living animal, that is hard, and so is changing one thing at a time.
scenes.visual: Fixed specimens: a row of fibres of different lengths, one fibre growing or old fibres becoming visible; then a living animal where it is hard to watch and change one factor; then a dish with a growing fibre.
scenes.narration: Every specimen Cajal studied was fixed. A row of fibres of different lengths could show stages of one fibre growing, or old fibres becoming visible. Someone had to watch a fibre while it was alive. Inside a living animal, that is hard, and so is changing one thing at a time.

scenes.tts: Take a piece of tissue at a chosen stage. Harrison removed frog neural tube before any nerve fibres could be seen. He set it in a drop of fresh adult frog lymph on a coverslip. The lymph clotted into a soft mesh that held the tissue. Then he inverted the coverslip over a hollow slide and sealed it. Tissue kept alive outside the body is an explant.
scenes.visual: Tissue piece cut from an embryo outline, set in a lymph drop on a coverslip, coverslip flipped over a hollow slide and sealed, lymph clots into a mesh, label explant.
scenes.narration: Take a piece of tissue at a chosen stage. Harrison removed frog neural tube before any nerve fibres could be seen. He set it in a drop of fresh adult frog lymph on a coverslip. The lymph clotted into a soft mesh that held the tissue. Then he inverted the coverslip over a hollow slide and sealed it. Tissue kept alive outside the body is an explant.

scenes.tts: In culture, cells need a solid to move on. Harrison saw frog cells wander along spider-web threads. To watch single neurons, break tissue into single cells and plate them thinly, so each can be followed. Banker and Cowan used fetal rat hippocampus, on polylysine-treated coverslips. Cells plated straight from tissue make a primary culture.
scenes.visual: Cells moving along web threads; tissue broken into single cells and plated sparsely on a polylysine coverslip; label primary culture.
scenes.narration: In culture, cells need a solid to move on. Harrison saw frog cells wander along spider-web threads. Cells plated straight from tissue make a primary culture.

scenes.tts: The medium is part of the experiment. Eagle found twelve amino acid compounds necessary for growth of Heela cells, a cell line. A continuous line can divide indefinitely. Partners can be added too. Isolated hippocampal neurons survived only a few days, but with hippocampal explants alongside, about two weeks. That is a coculture.
scenes.visual: Dish with medium list, HeLa line dividing; neurons alone fade after days, neurons with an explant alongside live about two weeks.

scenes.tts: To read a halo, look at the fibres around a ganglion after about a day. Their density shows how much factor a sample holds. The highest dilution that still gives a halo gives the activity. In this idealised example, the halo shrinks as the sample is diluted, and the most dilute dish gives none.
scenes.visual: Row of ganglia in dishes with dilutions; halos shrink; the last with a halo is marked as the activity; example tag.

scenes.tts: Culture can mislead. Mycoplasma escapes detection by turbidity or ordinary microscopy, and resists common antibiotics. Compare with mycoplasma-free lines. Identity can be wrong: Gartler reported apparent Heela contamination of other human lines in 1968. DNA fingerprinting by S T R profiling was reproducible between laboratories, across two hundred fifty-three lines. And a line differs from tissue: the Heela Kyoto genome shows extensive aneuploidy.
scenes.visual: Two panels: contamination invisible in a clear dish vs a clean control; line identity check (STR) and line vs tissue.
scenes.caption: Culture can mislead. Mycoplasma escapes detection by turbidity or ordinary microscopy, and resists common antibiotics. Compare with mycoplasma-free lines. Identity can be wrong: Gartler reported apparent HeLa contamination of other human lines in 1968. DNA fingerprinting by STR profiling was reproducible between laboratories, across 253 lines. And a line differs from tissue: the HeLa Kyoto genome shows extensive aneuploidy.

scenes.tts: In the early nineteen hundreds, Harrison watched fibres grow from tissue taken before fibres existed. The clot held no chain of cells, and some fibres arose from a single isolated cell. He concluded that an axon is drawn out from one cell. In the early nineteen fifties, in Rio de Janeiro, Levi-Montalcini cultured chick ganglia beside tumour fragments and saw a halo of fibres within a day. That halo became the bioassay used to purify nerve growth factor.
scenes.visual: Two panels: Harrison explant with a fibre from one isolated cell; Levi-Montalcini ganglion beside tumour fragment with a halo.

scenes.tts: In 2000, Shy-fella and colleagues found that neuroligin on a non-neuronal cell triggers presynaptic differentiation in contacting axons. A partner cell with no other synaptic machinery made that possible. Yet mice lacking neuroligins one to three had synapses in normal number in the brainstem, with impaired transmission. Keep this rule: sufficient in a dish does not mean required in the animal.
scenes.visual: Axon crossing a bare cell makes a terminal in a dish; then a knockout animal has normal synapses; rule box.
